scenario: Community search over short user-generated posts, questions, answers and comments. Key metrics are search relevance (nDCG) and CTR. Focus: semantic matching, query understanding, short-text retrieval, ranking models, and LLM applications in search.

papers.title: Is 2:4 Sparsity Still Worth It? Semi-Structured Sparsity versus Quantization in LLM Inference
papers.summary: An independent researcher compares "add 2:4 sparsity" versus "drop one precision tier" on Llama-3.1-8B-Instruct and Qwen3-8B under matched storage bits (including sparse indices) and matched nominal compute tiers, with measurements on L40S, H100, and RTX PRO 6000. ==As long as a lower precision is still available, adding 2:4 is both less accurate and slower==: 2:4 + INT8 costs the same storage as INT5. At the FP8 floor, a retrained 2:4 model served by vLLM on H100 raises prefill throughput 27% over dense FP8 with matched GSM8K; but ==during retraining perplexity recovers first while reasoning accuracy recovers much more slowly==.

deep_reading.title: Is 2:4 Sparsity Still Worth It? Semi-Structured Sparsity versus Quantization in LLM Inference

papers.title: SGLang Low-Latency Mode: Kernels and Runtime
papers.summary: SGLang, NVIDIA, and AMD use a plugin framework to plug specialized fused kernels into SGLang, cutting inter-kernel waits and cross-GPU communication at low concurrency. On AgentX replays of DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash + DSpark, per-user P90 generation rises from 671.2 to 928.4 token/s on 4×GB300 with 1 session, and from 331.6 to 516.0 token/s on 4×MI355X with 4 sessions. On NVIDIA, median time for one decode layer falls from 96.8 µs to 68.4 µs with almost the same kernel count; ==the speedup mainly comes from less waiting between kernels and overlapping work==.

deep_reading.title: SGLang Low-Latency Mode: Kernels and Runtime

papers.title: RCSD: Reinforcement and Continual Learning for Domain-Specific Speculative Decoding
papers.authors: Mingkang Liu, Weiming Meng, Peipei Jiao, Jiawei Zhang, Tianyuan Liu, Junyan Li, Lichen Pang
papers.summary: Hisense's RCSD continues training a speculative-decoding draft model that was distilled with HASS, using DPO or GRPO: sequences from the target alone are "good," sequences alternating target and draft are "bad," and the GRPO variant scores by acceptance rate. On Qwen3-1.7B and Llama-3.1-8B, acceptance length exceeds HASS on four datasets and draft steps 3–6—for example Qwen3-1.7B on GSM8K at step 6 rises from 2.176 to 3.246, and Llama-3.1-8B ShareGPT throughput from 142.3 to 176.6 token/s. ==The paper reports no generation-quality evaluation==.

deep_reading.title: RCSD: Reinforcement and Continual Learning for Domain-Specific Speculative Decoding

papers.title: UlaCache: Unified Logical Addressing for Sparse LLM Serving
papers.authors: Isaac Zhu, Alan Cao, Hugh Yin, Rocky Wang, Orion Wang, Hscos Zhang, Jack Li, Jason Zhao
papers.summary: Scitix.AI's UlaCache maps every GPU KV pool and CPU memory into one logical address space so ==GPU and CPU each store different history==, and removes MLA's cross-GPU duplication under TP; the GPU pool is shared across requests with a bucketed parallel LRU for eviction. Under SGLang + GLM-5.3 with 64K–128K inputs, concurrent decodeable requests on 8×B300 TP rise from HiSparse's 37 to 452; with speculative decoding, peak throughput is 1.16–2.51× HiSparse. At low concurrency latency is higher than pure-GPU SGLang.

deep_reading.title: UlaCache: Unified Logical Addressing for Sparse LLM Serving

papers.title: SPARE: Sparsity Allocation via Routing Entropy for Efficient MoEs
papers.authors: Yifan Yang, Hanling Yi, Dongquan Yang, Feng Lin, Rong Xiao, Aijun Li, Xiaotian Yu
papers.summary: Intellifusion's SPARE decides how many MoE experts to prune per layer: on calibration data it computes Top-K gate-weight entropy per token per layer, and ==layers whose weights are diffuse lose little when one expert is dropped, so they are pruned more==. It needs no training and composes with methods such as REAP that choose which experts to drop. Under the same selection method and budget, at 50% expert pruning Qwen3-30B-A3B's eight-task average rises from 57.2% to 63.8%, and DeepSeek-R1's math/code/science average from 80.1 to 82.8; on Mixtral it also beats uniform allocation.

papers.title: NormTune: Norm-Guided Parameter-Efficient Fine-Tuning for Reasoning-Intensive Tasks
papers.authors: Zhangming Li, Qinghao Hu, Weifan Guan, Yifan Zhang, Peisong Wang, Jian Cheng
papers.summary: CASIA finds that on reasoning tasks the ==weight-update norm of LoRA-style PEFT is far smaller than full fine-tuning==, and treats that as the main cause of the gap. NormTune adaptively amplifies under-updated layers by per-layer update norm. Training on S1K-1.1, rank-8 LoRA, Bone, and MoRA raise the average of AIME 2024, MATH 500, GPQA, and AIME 2025 by 24.24%, 11.33%, and 16.21%; at rank-256 all three match or slightly beat S1 full fine-tuning.

papers.title: FlashNext-RL: A System Optimization Study for Long-Horizon Agentic RL of Qwen3.8-Flash-Next
papers.summary: Snowflake specializes a training system for long-horizon software-engineering agent RL on Qwen3.8-Flash-Next, based on prime-rl, generating trajectories with vLLM and training the full 48-layer model in BF16 on one 8×B200 node (==freezing the first two layers and other parts==). After host offload, gradient accumulation, and MoE/sparse-attention kernel work, per-GPU training throughput rises from about 395 to 4,438 token/s and context from 32K to 131K. With three inference nodes, a 1,024-trajectory batch averages 22.4 minutes of real training per step.

papers.title: TrainBridge: Agentic NPU Training Optimization Guided by GPU Compilation Evidence
papers.authors: Yupeng Chen, Kunxiang Zhao, Xingjian Wang, Yue Zhao, Yijing Wu, Ye Liu, Kai Li, Congliang Chen, Ruoyu Sun
papers.summary: CUHK-Shenzhen and collaborators propose TrainBridge to optimize training programs on Ascend NPUs: ==it first extracts optimization intent from execution produced by a GPU compiler stack (operator fusion, etc.)==, lets an agent rewrite the NPU program, then iterates from NPU profiles. Across four workloads covering LLM pretraining, image classification, and vision–language training, mean speedup is 1.7×; on 27 Modded-NanoGPT speedrun records mean speedup is nearly 2.0×.

papers.title: Looped Uniform Diffusion Language Models
papers.authors: Saiteja Utpala, Chieh-Hsin Lai, Yuki Mitsufuji, Praneeth Vepakomma
papers.summary: MBZUAI and Sony study "looping" in uniform diffusion LMs (any position may be replaced by any token and can be revised during generation): reuse the first few Transformer layers inside each denoising step with the training objective and sampler unchanged. On OpenWebText and FineWeb-Edu, matching the validation NLL of a non-looped model trained on ~0.5T tokens takes up to 2.8× and 3.3× less training compute; at equal function-call counts generation perplexity is up to 9.8% lower. ==Sampling smaller loop counts more often during training== lets downstream tasks use 12% fewer loops without accuracy loss.

papers.title: Sparsity Should Be ALLOTted by Output: Training-Free Allocation of Block-Sparse Attention for Video Diffusion Transformers
papers.authors: Tianze Xia, Xiaoling Zhou, Ruya Lan, Yiqiao Liao, Chengru Song
papers.summary: CASIA and Keling propose ALLOT to decide how many blocks a video diffusion Transformer's block-sparse attention keeps for each layer × denoising step: measure each cell's effect on final video error, then jointly solve densities under a measured latency budget without changing the existing block-selection policy or kernels. The authors observe that ==the most sensitive layer–step pairs are nearly unchanged across inputs==. At equal or lower latency with XAttention it beats every compared allocation; on HunyuanVideo PSNR rises 11.8 dB; on four published Wan2.1, Wan2.2, and HunyuanVideo pipelines, all nine settings meet or beat the default allocation.
